title: Work limitation, care time, and health cost are linked research stages rather than one burden index
source_unit: Bounded cross-source comparison of SIPP monthly person transitions, ATUS standardized diary contrasts, and MEPS longitudinal health-cost outcomes; sources are not pooled

observations.period: 2024 reference year; SIPP resource-to-work transition by work-limiting status

denominator.unit: identified SIPP persons; valid adjacent pair universes vary by resource band and earnings/hours outcome

work_limiting_below_1x_hours_change.unit: percent; valid numeric hours pairs, Fay-BRR SE 2.547 pp

work_limiting_4x_hours_change.unit: percent; valid numeric hours pairs, Fay-BRR SE 0.629 pp

no_limitation_below_1x_hours_change.unit: percent; valid numeric hours pairs, Fay-BRR SE 0.745 pp

no_limitation_4x_earnings_change.unit: percent; valid numeric earnings pairs, Fay-BRR SE 0.276 pp

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month SIPP cross-lags using THINCPOV, TPEARN, TMWKHRS, and EDISABL with WPFINWGT and 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: This is a person-level descriptive transition layer. Earnings and hours use separate valid universes; change has no inferred direction and does not identify accommodation, job quality, care, or causality.
observations.subgroup: Reported work-limiting condition versus no reported condition, stratified by resource band.
observations.counterinterpretation: Different change shares can reflect composition, reporting, opportunity, earnings levels, hours preferences, or job mix rather than a work-limiting effect.

observations.period: 2024; ATUS richer-standardized eldercare-provider minus nonprovider contrast

denominator.unit: ATUS respondents in supported age-band × sex × labor-force-status × child × education cells; provider n=1,315

eldercare_difference_minutes.unit: standardized provider minus nonprovider minutes per diary day; SE 7.134

observations.method: ATUS 2024 diary aggregation with eldercare-roster provider status and standardization across supported demographic, labor-force, child, and education cells using replicate-weight variance.
observations.uncertainty: Provider status is descriptive and annual diary respondents are not a panel. The contrast does not identify care onset, intensity outside the diary, recipient outcome, employer response, health, or resource cause.
observations.subgroup: Eldercare providers versus nonproviders within supported standardization cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: Time differences can reflect unmeasured recipient need, distance, household support, employment choice, or provider selection; less work time is not automatically work loss.

denominator.unit: MEPS Panel 27 persons with positive longitudinal weight and valid paired fields

health_status_improved.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

health_status_worsened.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

out_of_pocket_expenditure_change.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

total_health_expenditure_change.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

employed_both_endpoint_rounds.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

employed_to_not_employed.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

not_employed_to_employed.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

wage_income_change.variance_method: Taylor linearization using LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU

observations.method: MEPS Panel 27 five-round longitudinal person analysis with positive longitudinal weights and paired health-status and expenditure fields.
observations.uncertainty: The panel measures health-cost co-movement, not care-time displacement or a causal effect of work limitation. Taylor-linearized precision uses LONGWT, VARSTR, and VARPSU; the normal intervals do not resolve expenditure skewness, attrition, nonresponse, or subgroup composition. Expenditure and out-of-pocket measures are distinct and are not household budget measures.
observations.subgroup: MEPS longitudinal persons with valid paired fields; income-stratified observations remain in the source record.
observations.counterinterpretation: Total health expenditure can rise while out-of-pocket spending falls, and health can improve or worsen without identifying a time, work, or care mechanism.

related_sources.claim: The SIPP work-limitation hours/earnings cross-lag supplies the monthly work/resource stage.
The ATUS provider-time layers supply care/time allocation context with composition controls.

boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled bridge. It places work/resource transitions, care-time allocation, and longitudinal health-cost change in one research architecture but does not observe the same person across SIPP, ATUS, and MEPS. It does not establish a care burden index, work-limitation effect, health-cost causation, household hardship, trust, political action, or remedy.
